newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks firm, blue chips hit new records.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks firm, blue chips hit new records.

text.p: Croatian stocks continued to firm with blue chips hitting new highs on Wednesday and traders expected the activity to pick up in earnest in future, further boosting share prices.

"I am optimistic about the coming period and wait for the credit rating," said Nenad Pavletic of Auctor brokerage, adding that even a lower rating than the investment grade "BBB" would give foreign buyers enough reason to invest in Croatia.
Three leading rating agencies are to announce their assessment sometime next week, probably around January 15.
Pavletic said the rating would help prop up prices of all liquid stocks and possibly other issues such as cable maker Elka and hotelier Riviera, traded from time to time on smaller volume.
Nine of 11 traded stocks on Wednesday rose, one fell and one remained unchanged.
Volume shrank to 9,217 from 12,032 units and turnover also fell to 5.2 million kuna.
Riviera led gainers, rising 39 kuna to 145 kuna from a month ago, but sold only 76 shares.
Most actively traded, Zagrebacka Banka, added 30 kuna to a new high of 1,230 kuna on volume of 3,080 units. Its 1/10 GDRs also topped earlier records, fetching $23.125 on London's Seaq.

The other fully-listed issue, Pliva pharmaceuticals, rose five kuna to 420 with 742 shares changing hands. Its GDRs, representing 1/5 of each shares after their 37-for-1 split, rose to $16.05 -- a new peak on the London Stock Exchange.
The day also saw new gains in other seaside hotel issues, including Laguna and Jadranturist. Both rose 50 kuna to 1,100 and 300 kuna respectively, with 105 and 511 shares traded.
The only loser was chocolate maker Kras, dipping 20 kuna down to close at 520 on volume of 464 shares.
